learn.title: Two places for data
learn.body: A running program mostly uses two areas of memory. The stack holds local variables and works automatically. The heap holds memory you ask for yourself while the program runs. The C standard does not use these words, but common systems all work this way.

learn.title: The stack
learn.body: Each function call gets its own space for its local variables. When the function returns, that space is released and the variables are gone. It is fast and needs no care from you, but it is limited in size and its contents cannot outlive the call.

learn.title: The heap
learn.body: When you need data that must outlive a function, or you only know its size while running, you ask for heap memory with `malloc`. It stays yours until you give it back with `free`. The cost is that you must remember to free it.

learn.title: One of each
learn.body: This prints `5 6`. `local` lives on the stack and disappears by itself. The block `heap` points at comes from `malloc` and must be freed. `heap` itself is a local pointer, the memory it points at is on the heap.

learn.title: Whose job is cleanup?
learn.body: Compare `int x = 1;` inside a function with `int *h = malloc(4);`.
steps: `x` is a local, so it is released on return
The block `h` points at is on the heap
Nothing frees it until you call `free(h)`
The pointer `h` itself is a local and vanishes on return

learn.body: Never return the address of a local variable from a function. Its stack space is released on return, so the pointer would refer to memory that is no longer yours.

questions.prompt: Where do ordinary local variables usually live?
questions.explanation: Locals are kept on the stack and released automatically when the function returns.
The heap does not clean itself. You must call `free`.

questions.prompt: Why is returning the address of a local variable a bug?
choices: Its memory is released when the function returns
questions.explanation: The pointer would be left pointing at released stack space.

questions.prompt: What does the example program print? Write it like `1 2`.
Match each property to the right place.
questions.explanation: Stack memory follows function calls. Heap memory follows your own malloc and free.
